hints: Distance covered is represented by the area under the velocity-time graph from $t = 0$ to $t = 42\text{ s}$.
Split this region into a triangular area from $t = 0$ to $t = 6\text{ s}$ and a rectangular area from $t = 6$ to $t = 42\text{ s}$, or treat the whole shape as a single trapezium.
walkthrough:
The total distance travelled on a velocity-time graph equals the area under the graph:
$$\text{Distance} = \text{Area under } v\text{-}t \text{ graph}$$

From $t = 0$ to $t = 6\text{ s}$, the graph forms a triangle of base $6\text{ s}$ and height $8.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8.2 = 3 \times 8.2 = 24.6\text{ m}$$

From $t = 6$ to $t = 42\text{ s}$, the sprinter runs at a constant speed of $8.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for a duration of $42 - 6 = 36\text{ s}$, forming a rectangle:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{rectangle}} = \text{width} \times \text{height} = 36 \times 8.2 = 295.2\text{ m}$$

Add the triangular and rectangular areas together:
$$\text{Distance} = 24.6 + 295.2 = 319.8\text{ m}$$

hints: Find the remaining distance to be covered in the final $10\text{ s}$ by subtracting $319.8\text{ m}$ from the total race distance of $400\text{ m}$.
The region from $t = 42$ to $t = 52\text{ s}$ is a trapezium with parallel sides $8.2$ and $V$, and height $\Delta t = 10\text{ s}$.
Set the area of this trapezium equal to the remaining distance and solve the linear equation for $V$.
walkthrough:
First, find how much distance remains in the race after the first $42\text{ s}$:
$$s_{\text{remaining}} = 400 - 319.8 = 80.2\text{ m}$$
The time elapsed in this final section is from $t = 42\text{ s}$ to $t = 52\text{ s}$, which gives $\Delta t = 52 - 42 = 10\text{ s}$.

The area under this section is a trapezium with parallel vertical sides of lengths $u = 8.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = V\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and width $10\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{u + v}{2} \times \Delta t = \frac{8.2 + V}{2} \times 10$$

Set this area equal to the remaining distance of $80.2\text{ m}$:
$$\frac{8.2 + V}{2} \times 10 = 80.2$$

Simplify $\frac{10}{2} = 5$ on the left side:
$$5(8.2 + V) = 80.2$$

Subtract $8.2$ from both sides to isolate $V$:
$$V = 16.04 - 8.2 = 7.84\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Deceleration is the rate of decrease of velocity, which is the negative gradient of the velocity-time graph.
Use the formula $d = \frac{u - v}{t}$ with initial speed $u = 8.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed $v = 7.84\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and time interval $t = 10\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
The formula for deceleration $d$ during uniform motion is the decrease in velocity divided by time taken:
$$d = \frac{u - v}{t}$$

Substitute the initial speed $u = 8.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed $v = 7.84\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and duration $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$d = \frac{8.2 - 7.84}{10}$$

Subtract the speeds in the numerator:
$$8.2 - 7.84 = 0.36$$

Divide by $10$ to find the final deceleration:
$$d = \frac{0.36}{10} = 0.036\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
